messages:
alex: quick thought — our SLO notify flow is still firing huge tenant storms when noisy signals align. proposes: a console 'noise curator' escape hatch to route noisy tenants to a low-priority lane + soft-rate-limit. cc @maya @devin
maya: +1. can you sketch minimal UX? we need discoverability and a reversible action (no infra deploys please)
devin: ideally it's just a toggle on the tenant card + a dropdown for fallback action: `suppress`, `route:ops-low`, `throttle-30s`
jen: picky: we need to persist policy server-side (per-tenant) and expose it to notify API. otherwise console toggles will be cosmetic
alex: agree. sketch: UI stores a `noise_curator` flag and `fallback` string. console calls `POST /api/tenants/:id/noise-curator` with body {"action": "route:ops-low", "ttl": 3600}
junior-dev: deploy-preview created for `notify-policy-ui` — link: https://staging.redwood/internal/preview/5621 :eyes:
maya: telemetry question — how do we tag incoming signals as "curation-eligible"? we don't want to misclassify real incidents
devin: heuristics: sustained high error-rate + high-instance-count + correlated across routes. we already compute `exposure_score` in signal pipeline. use threshold + a short cooldown
jen: we should expose the raw signal features in the console so reviewers can see why the curator suggested action (graphs: exposure, tenants affected, error types)
alex: agree. UX: small inline details panel with 3 sparklines + quick reasons. toggling curator shows a short modal with estimated reduction in alert volume (sampled sim)
maya: implementation concern — notify v2 uses per-route fanout. adding per-tenant escape hatch means notify should check tenant-level override first, then route fallback. cheap check: add `tenant_overrides` table and query early in fanout loop
devin: also need quota semantics: if we route to `ops-low` channel we still want to count for SLA burn (so we don't hide real burn). Maybe a flag `count_for_slo: true/false` on fallback
jen: +1 to counting for SLO; but we can set `alert_visibility: low` so console filters differently
alex: rollout plan idea: dark-launch the curator detection recommendation only (no action). show a banner in console for X tenants. collect acceptance rate. next, enable toggle in UI but default off. final: opt-in auto-curator
devin: tests: perf for notify path must not regress. the early tenant override check needs to be memcached and consistent across replicas
maya: telemetry: add a `curator_decision` tag to all signals so we can build a dashboard of TP/FP and false-suppression risk. also add an audit log entry every time a curator toggle is flipped
jen: api contract sketch:
POST /api/tenants/:id/noise-curator
{ "action": "route:ops-low", "ttl_seconds": 3600, "count_for_slo": true, "reason": "auto-suggest" }
returns 200 + audit id
alex: can someone prototype console wire and small API change? willing to pair on the wireframe
devin: i'll do the API server bit this week. will open a WIP PR in `eng-platform/notify` and add memcache integration
maya: i'll prototype the small modal — want the sparklines and the sampled simulation numbers
jen: i'll handle telemetry tags + audit log schema. quick Q: do we keep curator decisions in the same retention as other rules? might need longer retention for evals
alex: yes, keep curator_decision for 90 days at least
ops-bot: canary rollout for `notify-policy-ui` scheduled: tomorrow 08:00 UTC. I'll post results in #eng-platform
alex: perfect. follow-ups: devin open WIP PR, maya design mock, jen telemetry PR, we'll sync next Tue 9am. thanks :thumbsup:
